interpretations: "Above-average" means the status's mean modindex exceeds the overall mean modindex across all signals with non-null modindex (signal-level average). "How far above average" is the status mean minus that overall mean. "Differs from the mean of the qualifying statuses' averages" is the status mean minus the average of the qualifying statuses' means

"Above-average" means the status's mean modindex exceeds the unweighted mean of all statuses' mean modindex values (including the NULL group), rather than the signal-level overall mean. "How far above average" is the status mean minus that mean of group means. The difference from the qualifying mean is the status mean minus the average of the qualifying statuses' means

The comparison baseline is the overall mean modindex across all signals, including those whose rfistat is null. Null modindex values are excluded. "How far above average" is the status mean minus this baseline
"How far above average" is expressed as a ratio or percentage (status mean divided by overall mean, or percent above) instead of an absolute difference
"How it differs from the mean of the qualifying statuses' averages" is the signed difference (status mean minus qualifying mean), so it can be negative or positive
That same difference is taken as an absolute value (magnitude only)
The "mean of the qualifying statuses' averages" is the simple average of the qualifying statuses' mean modindex values (each status weighted equally)
The "mean of the qualifying statuses' averages" is a weighted average, i.e. the mean modindex across all signals belonging to the qualifying statuses pooled together
Signals with a null rfistat form their own group (shown as NULL or a label such as 'No Status' or 'Unknown'), and this group can qualify and appear in the output
Signals with rfistat = 'Unknown' are treated as the "no status" group, merged with NULL rfistat rows
Signals with rfistat = 'Unknown' are kept as a separate group from NULL rfistat rows
Empty-string rfistat values are treated as missing and grouped with NULL as the "no status" group
Statuses whose modindex values are all null are excluded entirely, since they have no average. Alternatively they are kept with a NULL average and fail the above-average test

The output has one row per qualifying status, with columns: status, average modindex, difference from the overall average, and difference from the qualifying mean. The overall average itself may or may not appear as an additional column
Results are ordered by average modindex descending, by status name, or left unordered
Values are left unrounded, so full floating-point precision is shown with no ROUND or formatting applied
Interpretations not yet covered:
The comparison baseline is the overall mean modindex across only signals with a non-null rfistat, excluding the no-status signals from the baseline
"Above-average" is inclusive (status mean greater than or equal to the overall mean) rather than strictly greater
rfistat values are normalized for case or surrounding whitespace before grouping (e.g. 'clean', 'Clean ' and 'CLEAN' count as one status)
"How it differs from the mean of the qualifying statuses' averages" is expressed as a ratio or percentage of the qualifying mean rather than an absolute difference
queries:
WITH overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(modindex) AS overall_avg
  FROM signals
  WHERE modindex IS NOT NULL
),
status_avg AS (
  SELECT rfistat, AVG(modindex) AS status_avg
  FROM signals
  WHERE modindex IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY rfistat
),
qualifying AS (
  SELECT s.rfistat, s.status_avg, o.overall_avg
  FROM status_avg s
  CROSS JOIN overall o
  WHERE s.status_avg > o.overall_avg
)
SELECT
  rfistat,
  status_avg,
  status_avg - overall_avg AS above_average_by,
  status_avg - (SELECT AVG(status_avg) FROM qualifying) AS diff_from_qualifying_mean
FROM qualifying
ORDER BY status_avg DESC;
WITH g AS (
  SELECT rfistat, AVG(modindex) AS m
  FROM signals
  GROUP BY rfistat
),
a AS (
  SELECT AVG(m) AS avg_m FROM g
),
q AS (
  SELECT g.rfistat, g.m, a.avg_m
  FROM g, a
  WHERE g.m > a.avg_m
)
SELECT rfistat,
       m - avg_m AS how_far_above_average,
       m - (SELECT AVG(m) FROM q) AS difference_from_qualifying_mean
FROM q;
SELECT rfistat,
       AVG(modindex) - (SELECT AVG(modindex) FROM signals) AS above_average
FROM signals
WHERE modindex IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY rfistat;
SELECT decodestat, AVG(decodeconf) / (SELECT AVG(decodeconf) FROM signaldecoding) AS ratio_to_overall_mean
FROM signaldecoding
GROUP BY decodestat;
